one_line: AI sector sees major funding rounds, new benchmarks, governance actions, and infrastructure expansions.

themes.title: AI startups secure major funding
themes.text: Hex Technologies announced a $100 million Series D round at a $1.2 billion valuation to launch Hex 4.0 for AI agents. Vera Health raised $28.5 million Series A, Casap secured $56 million Series B, Bites obtained $40 million Series A, Tutor Intelligence received $75 million Series B, and 42AI raised $62.5 million seed, expanding AI capabilities in health, finance, frontline training, robotics, and trading.

stories.headline: Hex Technologies raises $100 million Series D, launches Hex 4.0 for AI agents
Vera Health raises $28.5 million Series A to expand AI-powered clinical search platform
Casap raises $56 million Series B to expand AI dispute and fraud tools for banks
Bites raises $40 million Series A to expand AI‑driven frontline training platform
Tutor Intelligence raises $75 million Series B to expand robot model training and deployments
42AI emerges from stealth with $62.5 million seed to build behavioral world model

themes.title: New benchmarks gauge agentic AI
themes.text: SemiAnalysis released the GDPx benchmark testing 206 agentic tasks, where Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 achieved a 12 % average score. OpenAI introduced the LifeVal benchmark for everyday assistance tasks, and researchers demonstrated that GPT‑6 Astra edited 0.016 % of Qwen3.5‑0.8B weights to boost math performance sixfold; Google’s Suncatcher satellite ran the Gemma 4 model in orbit, returning its first AI response.

stories.headline: SemiAnalysis releases GDPx benchmark; Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 scores 12%
OpenAI launches LifeVal benchmark for AI assistance with everyday tasks
GPT-6 Astra edits 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B weights, boosting math performance sixfold
Google’s Project Suncatcher satellite generates first AI response in orbit

themes.title: Governance steps target AI content
themes.text: Anthropic updated Claude Code’s system prompt to forbid recreating existing video games, allowing only original or genre‑based games. The New York Times, New York Daily News, Chicago Tribune and Orlando Sentinel sued Brave Software for allegedly scraping their articles and providing them to AI firms, claiming paywall bypass.

stories.headline: Anthropic adds rule to stop Claude Code from cloning existing video games
New York Times and other papers sue Brave over AI scraping and paywall bypass

themes.title: AI firms expand infrastructure and tools
themes.text: OpenAI will combine the Chat and Work tabs in its desktop app for select users. Oracle announced a $20 billion stock and bond sale to fund AI data‑center expansion, Alphabet sold €6 billion in bonds with strong demand, Lumen and Microsoft expanded co‑selling for AI‑ready networks, OpenAI launched a Grid Protectors Program for utility power reliability, and SpaceX throttled Grok Bot usage citing high costs.

stories.headline: OpenAI to merge Chat and Work tabs in ChatGPT desktop app for select users
Oracle to raise $20 billion via stock and bond sales for AI data centers
Alphabet launches €6 billion euro‑denominated bond sale, €17 billion demand
Lumen and Microsoft expand co‑selling to deliver AI‑ready enterprise networks
OpenAI launches Grid Protectors Program to aid utilities with compute campus power reliability
Elon Musk throttles Grok Bot usage limits citing unsustainably high costs
